evidence.verdict: 4.0% of the catalogue can ever be recommended (187 of 4,734 products). The remaining 96.0% never clears minimum support, so no rule reaches them however a customer behaves. This is the popularity bias of Kathriarachchi et al. (2026) §3.2 measured rather than asserted, and it is a property of the support threshold, not a defect in the data.

evidence.verdict: 0.0% of the 319 products new to the hold-out window can be recommended by rules mined before they existed. A rule can only name products present when it was mined, so this is a structural limit of association rules rather than a result about this dataset: every new product is invisible to the method until the rules are mined again.

integration.note: 0 of 31 findings drew on more than one engine. Direct agreement is only possible where two engines speak about the same kind of subject, which on this configuration happens at business scope.
integration.limitation: The forecasting experiment targets total weekly revenue, so it produces no product-level signal and cannot corroborate a product pairing. Configuring a per-product forecast target would make that join available without changing this module.

components.revenue_at_stake: Share of the largest monetary quantity in the set. Zero where no monetary quantity could be attached.
components.evidence_weight: Reliability of the engine that produced the signal, computed from its out-of-sample performance.
components.corroboration: One where more than one engine spoke about the subject, zero otherwise. Only an integrated view can compute this term.

ranking.excluded: Margin contribution and inventory feasibility were proposed in Assessment One and are absent here, because Online Retail II records neither product cost nor stock level. A proxy would have made the score look more complete without making it more informative.

procedural_fairness.source: Wang, Huang, Tang & Yao (2026), Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research 85, Article 20, Definitions 1-3 and Equation 9.
procedural_fairness.verdict: Decisions of the same kind are driven by consistent evidence across all 1 templates assessed; the widest divergence is 0.00 on stock_and_display_together, within the declared threshold of 0.34.
procedural_fairness.method_note: An instantiation of their Definition 3 at the level of decision kinds, using the distance between driving-feature sets in place of maximum mean discrepancy over attribution values with a permutation test. Their measurement compares hundreds of matched individuals; this layer emits on the order of ten decisions, where a permutation test would return a p-value with nothing behind it. The substitution is a weakening and should be reported as one.
procedural_fairness.scope_note: Procedural fairness concerns the decision process. The distributive question, whether some customers receive materially better offers than others, is answered by the segment profiles and by the recommender hazard metrics, not here.

This is the popularity bias of Kathriarachchi et al. (2026) §3.2 measured rather than asserted, and it is a property of the support threshold, not a defect in the data.

structural_limits: The three lists cannot be ordered against one another, because the engines share no common scale.
No item can be marked as corroborated, since corroboration is a property of the join between lists.
Reliability is reported per engine and cannot be attached to an individual item from another engine.
No list can report which other engine was silent about a subject.
condition_b_isolated.note: Built from the same signals, the same thresholds and the same underlying runs as the integrated condition. Nothing is withheld; only the join is absent.

reconciliation_burden.note: The isolated condition presents 19 items across 3 lists with no ordering between them, so a reader comparing each item against the other lists performs 38 comparisons to reach the position the integrated condition starts from. Whether that cost matters is what the RQ4 sessions measure.

session_protocol.design: Within-participant. Each participant sees both conditions, with the order counterbalanced across participants so practice effects do not accumulate on one condition.
measures: Time to reach a stated stock or promotion decision
Recommendations accepted that the evidence does not support
Recommendations rejected that the evidence does support
Self-rated explanation sufficiency on a five-point scale
Self-rated trust in the presented analysis
session_protocol.measure_note: Acceptance is recorded as two separate counts rather than one rate. Jordan and Mitchell (2015) observe that a performance measure is a choice and may penalise one error direction more than the other; in retail, acting on a poor recommendation and ignoring a sound one carry different costs, and a single acceptance rate would average them away.
session_protocol.caveat: Both packs are text. Any difference observed is a difference of structure and content, not of visual design, which the dissertation should state when reporting the result.
